classes.name: AnimationSettings
classes.summary: Class for applying animations from the Human Generator library.
classes.description:
Animations are stored as rig independent clips and retargeted to the rig of this
human when set, see retarget.py. The result is a normal Blender action on the
rig, which can be edited like any other animation. Animations can also be added
as strips in the NLA editor, to chain or layer them.

When the human changes shape the actions are retargeted again, in place: only
the channels of the animated bones are written again, other channels, the name
and fake user of the action and the NLA strips using it are kept.

members.summary: The active action created by Human Generator on the rig, if any.

members.name: strips
members.summary: NLA strips on the rig with an animation created by Human Generator.

members.summary: All actions created by Human Generator on the rig, active and in strips.

members.name: is_active
members.summary: True if a Human Generator animation is on this human, active or in NLA.

members.name: loop
members.summary: True if the active animation repeats outside its frame range.

members.name: finger_curl
members.summary: Blend of the fingers between the rest pose (0) and the animation (1).

members.name: frame_count
members.summary: Number of keyed frames of the active animation, 0 if there is none.

members.name: set
members.summary: Applies an animation from the Human Generator library to this human.
members.description:
By default the animation becomes the active action of the rig, replacing
the active Human Generator animation set before, and the pose of the body.
The pose of the face rig is kept. Keys are placed on whole scene frames,
resampled if the frame rate of the clip differs from the scene.

With `as_strip` the animation is added as a strip in the NLA editor instead,
after the last strip added this way. An active Human Generator animation
is pushed down to a strip first, so the new one is visible.

params.name: preset
params.description: Name of the animation to set, you can get options from the `get_options` method.

params.name: context
params.description: Context to use. Defaults to None.

params.name: loop
params.description: Repeat the animation outside its frame range. Defaults to the setting of the clip, True for cyclic animations.

params.name: set_frame_range
params.description: Set the frame range of the scene to the animation. Defaults to True. Ignored for strips.

params.name: finger_curl
params.description: Blend of the fingers between the relaxed hand of the rest pose (0) and the hand of the animation (1). Defaults to 1.0.

params.name: as_strip
params.description: Add as NLA strip instead of as active action. Defaults to False.

params.name: frame_start
params.description: Scene frame of the first key. Defaults to the start frame of the scene, for strips to the end of the last Human Generator strip.

returns.description: Optional[bpy.types.Action]: The created action, None if preset is "none".

raises.description: If the human has a Rigify rig.

classes.name: ProcessSettings
classes.summary: Processes the human for export, as the Process tab does, or step by step.
classes.description:
`run` does everything the Process tab does, from an `ExportSettings`:

    settings = ExportSettings.from_recipe("unity")
    settings.output.folder = "/path/to/project/Assets/Characters"
    result = human.process.run(settings)
    print(result.files)

The other methods are the single steps of `run`, which change this human in
place, so call them on a `human.duplicate()`. They take the section of the
settings they are about, or plain arguments. `run` does them in this order,
which the steps depend on:

    1. `set_shape_keys`, so the other steps only carry the keys that stay
    2. `convert_to_haircards`
    3. `convert_to_game_eyes` and `lod.set_teeth_lod`, before baking, as
       they change the materials
    4. `bake_textures`, before the meshes are reduced
    5. `set_quality` (or `lod.set_body_lod` and `lod.set_clothing_lod`)
    6. `remove_hidden_skin`
    7. `set_t_pose_as_rest` and `convert_to_game_rig`
    8. `apply_names`
    9. `prepare_clips`, once the skeleton is final
    10. `human.export.write`, or `mark_as_processed` to keep it in the file

The steps that change the human for good refuse to run twice, see the
`has_*` and `was_*` properties.
